clue.text: One should auger best of all, and want to get started…

definitions.text: One should auger best of all
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: a champion at the drill bit, the best of all at boring with an auger
second meaning: the idiom for being impatient to begin, like a horse chewing its bit

explanation.surface: A boring tool should drill best of all and be raring to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: An auger is a drill, and its cutting end is the bit; a champ at the bit is the best driller. The idiom, more often 'champing at the bit', means restless to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ at the bit is an idiom for being impatient to start, from a restless horse chewing on its bridle.

clue.text: Proves a nuisance when her airs alter it.

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so the letters of her airs are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's airs and graces become irritating once they shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester or keep troubling them, so the word means making oneself a nuisance.

clue.text: Tom might be in a state, briefly, having the habit.

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri, a US state
using describes someone with a drug habit

explanation.surface: A man called Tom may be in some state, addicted to something.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is not a man but a tomcat, and what a cat might be doing is hunting mice; 'having the habit' means taking drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male cat, and mousing, hunting mice, is just what one might be busy doing.

clue.text: How one behaves in the evening?

definitions.text: How one behaves in the evening?

parts.words: How one behaves in the evening?
parts.note: a cryptic definition: evening means getting even, settling a score, not the time after sunset

explanation.surface: A question about how someone acts at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' looks like the time of day, but here it is 'even-ing', getting even with somebody.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes revenge for a wrong evens the score, and that is exactly what one who avenges does.

clue.text: An acute ache really shows up the head of the class!

indicators.note: the answer shows up, appearing within the letters of acute ache really

parts.note: the letters run on in sequence across acute ache really, from the T of acute to the R of really

explanation.surface: A sharp pain really exposes the top pupil in the room!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows up' means the answer appears inside the words An acute ache really. The head of the class looks like the top pupil; it is the person standing at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The teacher is the person in charge of a class of pupils, and so at its head.

clue.text: Gets up to look around what we all were, and gets dressed.

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means going upward, so the letters are read from bottom to top
the word for look goes around the word for what we all were

parts.note: to see is to look
every one of us was once born

explanation.surface: Someone rises, looks round at what we used to be, and puts on clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets up' reads like getting out of bed, but in a down clue it means writing letters upward: 'around' puts the look word round the birth word to make SEBORNE, and that is read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrobe is to put on a robe or clothing, so one who enrobes gets dressed.

clue.text: It might be necessary to get a second-hand organ.

definitions.text: It might be necessary to get a second-hand organ

parts.words: It might be necessary to get a second-hand organ
parts.note: a cryptic definition: a donor organ is second-hand, and must be surgically put in

explanation.surface: Buying a used church organ might take some arranging.
explanation.walkthrough: A second-hand organ sounds like a used musical instrument; it is a body part from a donor.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons implant a donated organ, so the operation is needed for a patient to receive one.

clue.text: If the radio program drifts, it might be the direction of the speaker is wrong, getting this.

definitions.text: If the radio program drifts, it might be the direction of the speaker is wrong, getting this

parts.words: If the radio program drifts, it might be the direction of the speaker is wrong, getting this
parts.note: a cryptic definition: a talk show that wanders from its topic, its speaker heading the wrong way

explanation.surface: A radio show losing its signal, as if the loudspeaker were pointing the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: Drifting and the speaker's direction suggest a radio losing its station and a loudspeaker; really a talker is drifting away from the topic.
explanation.definitionFit: Being off the subject means wandering from the topic under discussion, as a rambling speaker does.

clue.text: Fish stories might be, but mumps make it.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an angler's exaggerated tale is hard to believe
second meaning: the swollen glands of mumps make it painful to swallow

explanation.surface: Anglers' yarns might be tall tales, though an illness can be blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: A fish story is the American name for a tall tale, especially one about the size of a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard to swallow is both an idiom for difficult to believe and a literal description of throat swelling.

clue.text: …and one might augur well, if told to be good.

definitions.text: and one might augur well, if told to be good

parts.words: and one might augur well, if told to be good
parts.note: a cryptic definition: this is something that is told by a teller, and if it is a good one it promises well

explanation.surface: It continues 1 Across: someone told to be good might show promise.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue carries on the sentence from 1 Across, and 'told to be good' sounds like an order to behave. It really means that when this is told, by a teller, it may turn out good.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller tells what lies ahead, and good luck foretold in that way is a hopeful omen.

clue.text: A parent is about to hold the winner at Actium.

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so A and the parent go round the word for hold

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to grip is to hold

explanation.surface: A mother or father is about to grasp the victor of an ancient sea battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is about' says A and PA go round the word for 'to hold'. Actium (31 BC) is usually credited to Octavian, but his admiral Marcus Agrippa commanded the fleet that beat Antony and Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was the Roman general who led Octavian's navy to victory in the battle off Actium.

clue.text: Following one of the things that make residue?

definitions.text: one of the things that make residue
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the waste left after ore is processed, so one of them is a piece of residue

explanation.surface: Someone tracking one of the components of leftover sludge.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning stretches the mining word 'tailings', usually plural, to a single one; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailing means shadowing or trailing a person, and tailings are the refuse residue of mining and milling.

clue.text: The main turning point to one rhyming with squash.

parts.note: the hub is the central part a wheel turns on; main here means central, not the sea
a bard is a poet, someone who writes in rhyme

explanation.surface: The sea's turning point leading to a word that rhymes with squash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' tempts towards the sea and 'rhyming with squash' towards a word that rhymes with it; in fact the poet is the rhymer and squash is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubbard is a variety of winter squash, a large, hard-skinned type of pumpkin-like vegetable.

clue.text: Standards set by junior officers.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flags, banners carried as standards
second meaning: an ensign is the lowest commissioned rank in the US Navy

explanation.surface: Rules of conduct laid down by low-ranking officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standards set' reads as rules being laid down; standards here are flags.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is both a flag flown by a ship and the most junior commissioned naval officer.

clue.text: Dish that returns the title to the emperor.

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the title is read backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title given to a knight
Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors, such as Otto the Great

explanation.surface: A dish that gives an honour back to an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns the knight's title back to front as RIS. Several Holy Roman Emperors were called Otto, and crosswords use the name for an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in broth.

clue.text: How some bad nails are not stored away.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ragged fingernails have not been smoothed with a nail file
second meaning: papers not put away in a filing system

explanation.surface: Why some crooked nails were left out of the toolbox.
explanation.walkthrough: Bad nails suggests carpentry; they are fingernails, and the two senses come from two kinds of filing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfiled covers both nails that were never smoothed down and documents never put into their folders.

clue.text: Hospital patients might be so headed, as one makes an advance.

definitions.text: Hospital patients might be so headed
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: patients are headed for a ward
second meaning: moving onward or ahead

explanation.surface: Sick people might be heading this way as someone moves on.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the answer into two words: patients go 'for ward'.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward means onward or ahead, the direction someone goes when progressing.

clue.text: Was the speech of the Spartans?

definitions.text: Was the speech of the Spartans?

parts.words: Was the speech of the Spartans?
parts.note: a cryptic definition: the Spartans of Laconia were famous for terse speech

explanation.surface: A history question about how Spartans talked.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparta was in the region of Laconia, and its people were famed for few words; the English word for terse comes from there.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic means using very few words, after the Laconians, the Spartans known for their brevity.

clue.text: What the fastest gunman gets to allow a tiny bit of water in the fall.

definitions.text: a tiny bit of water in the fall

parts.note: in Westerns the quickest gunfighter gets the drop on his opponent, drawing first
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A Western gunslinger permitting a little water into a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the fall' sounds like autumn or a waterfall, but it means a falling bit of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A droplet is a very small drop of liquid, such as one falling from a tap or the sky.

clue.text: Jack-low combination, but you might need more than one shot with it.

definitions.text: you might need more than one shot with it

indicators.note: a combination is a mixing together, so the letters of jack and low are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A low-slung jack combined into one tool, though a single try may not do the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combination' suggests a lock's code, and 'shot' a gunshot or drink. It asks for an anagram of JACKLOW, and the shots are injections.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is the common name for tetanus, which is prevented by a course of vaccine injections and boosters.

clue.text: Found and ate cold hash.

indicators.note: making a hash of something is jumbling it, so the letters of ate cold are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone discovered cold leftovers and ate them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold hash' looks like a cold dish; hash is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Found and located are synonyms, both meaning discovered where something was.

clue.text: Old Indian or French name for an animal.

parts.note: the Caribs were an indigenous people of the Caribbean islands
ou is the French word for or

explanation.surface: An animal's name could come from an old Native American or French source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like it joins two options; it is a word to translate into French.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a large deer of the far north.

clue.text: With such, is the up-keep criticized?

definitions.text: With such, is the up-keep criticized?

parts.words: With such, is the up-keep criticized?
parts.note: a cryptic definition: keeping up with these neighbours is the much-mocked habit of matching their lifestyle

explanation.surface: Asks whether people are criticised for the maintenance costs of some property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up-keep' looks like maintenance, but the hyphen splits it into 'keeping up'; keeping up with the Joneses is mocked as status-seeking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Joneses are the proverbial neighbours whose possessions people try to match, an idiom for social one-upmanship.

clue.text: Just a tumble-down place of spiritual association.

definitions.text: Just a tumble-down place of spiritual association

parts.words: Just a tumble-down place of spiritual association
parts.note: a cryptic definition: a city famous for walls that fell, and for the spiritual song about its battle

explanation.surface: A ruined spot where people once met for religious fellowship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spiritual' is not about the soul: it is the African American spiritual 'Joshua Fit the Battle of Jericho', in which the walls came tumbling down.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the walls of this city fell at the trumpets of Joshua's army, as the well-known spiritual song tells.

clue.text: One aspect of Locarno pertains to a kind of luminous light.

definitions.text: pertains to a kind of luminous light

indicators.note: another aspect of a word is a different arrangement of the same letters, so Locarno is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something about the Swiss lakeside town has to do with a glowing light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One aspect of' signals a rearrangement of LOCARNO, a Swiss town on Lake Maggiore. The definition is a whole phrase for an adjective relating to a corona, the glowing ring around the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Coronal is the adjective for a corona, the halo of glowing light seen around the sun or moon.

clue.text: The band may carry the show, but it's frequently changed.

definitions.text: The band may carry the show
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a broadcast travels on this frequency band
second meaning: viewers flick between these constantly, and a frequency is just what changes

explanation.surface: A musical group might make a stage show a success, though its line-up keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: The band looks like musicians carrying a show; it is a band of radio frequencies, and 'frequently' slyly nods to frequency.
explanation.definitionFit: A television channel is a frequency band carrying programmes, and viewers switch between them all the time.

clue.text: Sauce that could be taken by degrees in a tortilla.

indicators.note: something taken in is absorbed into the middle, so the degrees go inside the tortilla
in places the degrees within the folded tortilla

parts.note: a taco is a tortilla folded around a filling
BAs are Bachelor of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: A sauce eaten a little at a time inside a Mexican flatbread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By degrees' reads as gradually; here degrees are BAs, and 'taken' with 'in' puts them inside the taco.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a brand of hot pepper sauce, often shaken over Mexican food.

clue.text: A flier that went to school? (It should take experience to make one.)

definitions.text: A flier that went to school
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: taking a flier is having a guess, and one that went to school is educated

definitions.text: It should take experience to make one
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a guess based on knowledge and experience

explanation.surface: A pilot who was trained, which takes experience to become.
explanation.walkthrough: A flier sounds like a pilot or a bird, but in American English to take a flier is to take a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: An educated guess is an estimate grounded in knowledge, the kind that experience lets you make.
